need: One flashcard state must have one dominant message owner. Read-only history and answer entitlement may both affect behavior, but they must converge into a coherent hierarchy instead of producing adjacent accent surfaces with competing or contradictory claims.
negativeBoundary: Do not stack two full-width accent notices for the same card state, do not say that an answer is being viewed while also saying it cannot be viewed, and do not show self-grading guidance when a persisted read-only card cannot be graded.
acceptanceCriteria: The card renders at most one dominant state notice for the combined read-only and answer-entitlement state.
The notice title, body and available controls describe one coherent action model without contradictory claims.
Secondary read-only context is reduced to subordinate copy or metadata when the entitlement notice is dominant.
Accent treatment is reserved for one focal state; unavailable or historical context does not compete at equal emphasis.
UAT covers available, unavailable, read-only, and read-only-plus-unavailable state combinations.

accepts: One state surface whose hierarchy explains both access and historical read-only behavior.
Context-specific copy that mentions only actions the learner can still take.
rejects: Two adjacent pink surfaces with equal emphasis for one card state.
The simultaneous claims 'answer unavailable' and 'viewing saved answer'.

review.rationale: Approved after desktop and compact UAT proved one dominant neutral unavailable-answer surface with subordinate read-only context and no competing accent notice.
